chapter: Kid Rena, Kelly and the old trumpeters
title: Manuel Perez's funeral parades and today's parades
summary: Perez was the favorite funeral-parade leader; the two compare how often funeral bands still play, mentioning Kid Howard.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Tell me a little more about Manuel Perez when you heard his band. Where was it? Economy Hall?

Well I used to hear Manuel's band most of the times. He seemed to have been the favorite band leader for these funeral parades and whatnot. Well how long? Because that used to be customary every time some member of some society had passed and they used to always have a funeral band.
But they're not as frequent as they used to be.
Well there'd be maybe two a week almost.
We don't hear about all of them but there was one a week ago today. Uh-huh. Kit Howard, I don't know if you remember. Yeah I used to work with Kit Howard.
He had one last Sunday afternoon. I worked with Kit Howard. I wasn't there. I left town.
A friend wrote me this week and said he found me.

There were three parades last Sunday. One across the river and then two over on the side. Is that right? And then in addition to that there was Kit Howard at the funeral. Is that right? Well anyhow I used to remember Manuel Perez because he was always so powerful.
